implementation_statement: Access control policy POL-02 (2024) was re-approved by the Board Risk Committee on 2026-09-15 (P06). Procedures exist for the payments hub and online banking admin console; the core role-template procedure is due 2027-03-31 (gap 4).

provider_if_inherited: Identity provider; core processor; digital banking provider
implementation_statement: Workforce accounts are created from HR tickets and federated through the identity provider to the payments hub, the admin console, and the cloud accounts. Core accounts are created by the core security administrators in the core security module. Managers review payments hub and admin console access quarterly. Gaps: core entitlements are not tied to role templates (26% of sampled teller and universal banker users exceed their role, gap 4; R-006); transfers do not trigger removal of prior core roles (R-040).
evidence: HR tickets; IdP export; core user and role export; quarterly review records (Q1 and Q2 2026)

implementation_statement: Joiner and leaver events flow automatically from the HR system to the identity provider, which disables federated access at termination. The core and the correspondent portal vendor accounts are not connected to this automation.
Identity provider accounts inactive for 60 days are disabled automatically. Core accounts have no inactivity disable; a quarterly report is reviewed manually.
evidence: IdP policy; core inactive user report

implementation_statement: Account creation, modification, enabling, disabling, and removal are logged in the identity provider and the core security module; identity provider events go to the SIEM.
evidence: IdP audit log; core security audit report

implementation_statement: Role-based access is enforced in the core (212 roles), the payments hub (wire entry, wire approval, template maintenance, correspondent operations, and administration roles), and the admin console (help desk, treasury, administrator). Business users receive entitlements set by the customer administrator within bank-set limits.
evidence: Role matrices; payments hub role export

implementation_statement: The production account accepts traffic only from the shared network hub. The payments workstations sit on an isolated segment that can reach only the Federal Reserve connection and the payments hub.
evidence: Network diagrams (P04); firewall and security group rules

implementation_statement: Maker-checker is enforced for every outgoing wire, and beneficiary template maintenance is a separate role from wire approval. Gap: the 6 payments hub application administrators can change approval limits and callback settings without a second person (R-027).
evidence: Payments hub role matrix; configuration change log

implementation_statement: Standard users have no local administrator rights. Gaps: excess core entitlements (gap 4); 6 payments hub administrators hold full rights for routine support.

Security functions in the identity provider and cloud accounts are limited to named security and cloud administrators. Core security administration is held by 5 IT staff, 2 of whom also process account maintenance.
Directory and cloud administrators use separate privileged accounts through PAM. Core security administrators and payments hub administrators use their everyday accounts (gap 4; R-007).
Privileged accounts for the directory and cloud are vaulted with just-in-time elevation. Not yet covered: core security administrators, payments hub and correspondent portal administrators (R-007).
Privileged use is logged for the directory, identity provider, and cloud accounts and sent to the SIEM. Payments hub and core administrator actions are logged but not sent to the SIEM (gap 7).
The identity provider locks workforce accounts for 15 minutes after 10 failed attempts. The digital banking provider locks customer sign-ins after 5 failed attempts and requires an out-of-band reset.
Teller and payments workstations lock after 5 minutes idle; other endpoints after 10 minutes, enforced by device management.

provider_if_inherited: Digital banking provider; payments hub vendor
implementation_statement: Customer online banking sessions end after 10 minutes idle; admin console, payments hub, and correspondent portal sessions after 15 minutes.
Remote access to bank systems is allowed only through the identity provider with MFA and a compliant bank-managed device. The payments workstations cannot be reached remotely.
Remote sessions are logged by the identity provider and the remote access gateway and monitored by the MSSP.
Personal devices may reach email only through a managed app with data controls. Vendor support staff connect to the payments hub from vendor systems through a standing vendor VPN (R-048).
evidence: Mobile app policy; vendor VPN list

implementation_statement: Awareness and training requirements are in POL-05 (P06), re-approved 2026-09-15.
Annual security awareness training for all staff, monthly phishing simulations (June 2026 click rate 5.9%), and monthly reminders.
Training covers phishing and pretext calls. Gap: it does not cover requests to change customer contact information or voice impersonation of customers (R-028).
Wire room and treasury operations staff complete annual payment-fraud training. Branch and contact center staff who process contact-information changes have no role-based fraud training (gap 2).
Logging requirements are in POL-03 statement 4.3; the logging and monitoring standard (STD-02) is due 2027-01-31 (gap 11).

provider_if_inherited: Core processor; digital banking provider; cloud provider
implementation_statement: Logged events are defined for the identity provider, cloud accounts, endpoints, and firewalls. Payments hub and correspondent portal event types are not defined for security review (gap 7).
Payments hub audit records include user, role, action, wire reference, amount, beneficiary, timestamp, and workstation.

control_name: Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
implementation_statement: The MSSP reviews SIEM alerts 24x7. Payments operations reviews a daily wire exception report. Gaps: no review or alerting on beneficiary, template, limit, or contact-information changes; core security reports are not reviewed monthly (gap 7; R-013).
evidence: MSSP monthly reports; daily exception report

implementation_statement: Identity, endpoint, firewall, and cloud logs are correlated automatically in the SIEM. Payments hub and core logs are not integrated.
Logs from all cloud accounts land in a write-once bucket in the security and log archive account, administered only by the security team.
SIEM keeps 1 year searchable; the log archive keeps 3 years. Payments hub logs stay in the application for 90 days (gap 7).
The payments hub, admin console, core, identity provider, and cloud services generate audit records by default.
The co-sourced IT audit firm performs an annual independent assessment (P07, 2026-08-03 to 2026-08-21) and the annual penetration tests; results go to the Audit Committee.

Interconnections with the core processor, the digital banking provider, and the Federal Reserve are covered by agreements. The respondent agreements (2019) set no security, availability, or incident notice terms (gap 12).
POA&M items are tracked in the GRC tool and reported to the Audit Committee each quarter (P07 poam.csv).
Monthly key risk indicators are reported to the CRO. Continuous monitoring does not yet include payments hub configuration or third-party performance metrics.

baseline: Not in Moderate baseline (selected by tailoring)
implementation_statement: Selected by tailoring: annual external and internal penetration tests by an independent firm, including the payments hub and correspondent portal from the internet and from a branch network.
Configuration management requirements are in POL-01 and POL-04; the configuration standard (STD-01) is due 2027-03-31 (gap 11).

Cloud accounts use infrastructure-as-code templates and organization guardrails. Endpoint and server baselines are informal; payments hub configuration (limits, callback fields, approval rules) has no documented baseline.
Infrastructure and application changes go through the change advisory board. Payments hub business configuration (limits, approval rules) is changed by administrators outside change control (R-047).
evidence: Change tickets; payments hub configuration log

implementation_statement: Cloud posture management checks accounts against a benchmark daily. Server and endpoint settings are not measured against a benchmark (gap 11).
Payments workstations run only the Federal Reserve access software and the browser allowlist; unused services are disabled on the payments hub servers.
Hardware and software inventory from device management, cloud inventory, and network discovery, reconciled monthly.
Users cannot install software; application allowlisting on teller and payments workstations.
Business continuity policy (2025) and POL-04 statement 4.7 cover backup and recovery.

provider_if_inherited: Core processor; digital banking provider; cloud provider
implementation_statement: The business continuity plan covers branches, the contact center, and wire rooms, with the Georgia alternate site. Gaps: recovery objectives for correspondent services and the item processing servers are not in the plan; recovery roles for the payments hub failover are not documented (gap 6).
The plan references the core processor and digital banking provider plans, but not the incident response plan or the respondent institutions.
Wire room staff train on the alternate procedure each year; correspondent operations and IT recovery staff have no contingency training.

The bank participates in the core processor disaster recovery test each year. The payments hub failover was tested once (2025) and took 9 hours against a 4-hour RTO; no corrective action was tracked (gap 6; R-004).
evidence: 2025 failover test report; core processor test letter

implementation_statement: Backups are stored in the backup account in a second region with write-once retention and separate administrator credentials.
The second cloud region is the alternate processing site for the payments hub; the Georgia regional office is the alternate operations site. Neither has been proven at full volume (gap 6).
Dual carriers at both operations sites and to the core processor; cellular backup at each branch.
Daily backups of production workloads with 35-day write-once retention; on-premises servers back up to an appliance that replicates nightly to the backup account.
File-level restores are tested monthly. Full restores of the payments hub database and the item processing servers have not been tested.
Recovery runbooks exist for the directory and cloud networking. Payments hub reconstitution and reconciliation steps (matching sent wires to hub records after failover) are not written.
Identification and authentication requirements are in POL-02 (P06).
Every workforce user has a unique identity in the identity provider; core logons are unique per user.
Privileged accounts use phishing-resistant hardware keys for the identity provider, directory, and cloud accounts.
All workforce users use MFA (authenticator app with number matching).
Workforce authentication uses replay-resistant protocols (federated tokens and app-based MFA).
Identifiers are assigned from HR records and never reused.

Workforce passwords must be 14 characters and are checked against a banned list. Gaps: the core allows 8-character passwords; 2 vendor-created generic administrator accounts in the correspondent portal were still enabled (P07; R-049).
Banned-password checks apply in the identity provider; the core password policy is weaker and is managed through the core security module.

Business users must use MFA (app or SMS codes). Consumers get an SMS code only on new-device sign-in. New beneficiaries are not confirmed out of band, and 12% of business users are on SMS codes (gap 3; R-002, R-016). Respondent users sign in to the correspondent portal through the customer identity service with app-based MFA.
evidence: Provider MFA enrollment report; customer identity service policy

implementation_statement: New customers are identified under the customer identification program. Contact-information changes are not re-verified out of band (gap 2; R-001).
Incident response policy POL-03 re-approved 2026-09-15 (P06).
The IT and security teams train on the plan each year; executives, branch managers, and correspondent operations have not been trained on their roles.
A technical ransomware tabletop was held in 2025 with IT only. No executive or fraud scenario exercise has been held (gap 8).
The MSSP detects and contains endpoint and identity threats 24x7; the ISO leads handling. Fraud cases run separately in the BSA case system and are not linked to security incidents.
Security incidents are tracked in the incident register; payment-fraud events are tracked only in the BSA case system.

The plan includes the 36-hour OCC notice (12 CFR 53.3). Gaps: no determination criteria, no Federal Reserve notice for the holding company, and no outbound notice to respondent banks (gap 8; R-008, R-009).
The MSSP incident response team and the cyber insurer panel (breach counsel, forensics) are available on retainer.
Incident response plan (2024), updated by the P08 runbooks approved 2026-09-18. It has not been distributed to branch managers, correspondent operations, or the MSSP in its new form.
Payments hub vendor support connects through a standing VPN with named accounts and MFA; sessions are not approved per session or recorded (R-048).
Drives are wiped or destroyed by a certified vendor with serial-number certificates, including ATM drives.
Access to the wire rooms, operations center, and server room is authorized by the COO and reviewed quarterly.
Badge readers and cameras on the wire rooms, operations center, and server room; visitor logs.
Policies POL-01 to POL-05 are reviewed annually and were re-approved on 2026-09-15.
This SSP, approved 2026-09-18, is reviewed annually and after major changes.
Rules of behavior (POL-05) acknowledged at hire and each year (98% for 2026).

baseline: Not in Moderate baseline (selected by tailoring)
implementation_statement: Selected by tailoring. The written information security program is approved by the board (III.A.1); last approved October 2025; updated program scheduled for 2026-10-20.

baseline: Not in Moderate baseline (selected by tailoring)
implementation_statement: Selected by tailoring. The ISO is designated by the board, reports to the CRO, and has a direct line to the Board Risk Committee. The ISO team also runs vulnerability scanning and MSSP triage, so internal audit tests those controls independently.

baseline: Not in Moderate baseline (selected by tailoring)
implementation_statement: Selected by tailoring. The enterprise risk appetite (2025) is qualitative for cyber risk; measurable cyber tolerances are proposed in P01 for board approval on 2026-10-20 (gap 1; R-012).
Background and credit checks before hire for all employees, and again before transfer into the wire rooms or IT administration.

HR opens termination tickets on or before the last day; federated access is disabled automatically. Core access is removed manually; 9 of 25 sampled terminations had core access removed after the last day (R-039).
Transfers create an HR ticket but do not trigger a review of prior core roles (R-040).
Contractors with system access sign confidentiality terms and follow POL-05.
Sanctions procedure in POL-01 statement 4.8; HR documents each sanction.
Information is classified under POL-04; the COBP is categorized Moderate (section 6).
Annual risk assessment with NIST SP 800-30 tables (P01, 2026-07-24), including payment fraud, third parties, and AI.
Critical vendors are risk-rated at onboarding and annually; fourth parties (subservice organizations) are not assessed.

Monthly authenticated scans of servers, endpoints, and cloud workloads by the MSSP; annual penetration tests. Gap: 18% of on-premises servers missed the 30-day critical patch target in the first half of 2026 (R-015).
Risk responses are recorded in the register with owners and dates, and accepted at the levels in POL-01 statement 4.4.
Critical components identified in the BIA (P05): payments hub, core connectivity, identity provider, payments workstations.
Contracts for new services include security and confidentiality terms. 9 critical vendor contracts set no incident notice time frame (gap 5; R-010).
Critical vendors are tiered and their SOC reports collected each year. CUECs are mapped only for the core processor; 53.4 contacts were given to 3 of 7 bank service providers (gap 5; R-011).
14 item processing servers run an unsupported operating system. They are isolated on their own segment with restricted access; replacement is in the 2027 plan (gap 10; R-014).
Denial-of-service protection for online banking and the correspondent portal is provided by the providers edge services.
Next-generation firewalls at the edge and the cloud network hub; branch networks separate teller, back office, and guest traffic; payments workstations are isolated.

control_name: Deny by Default, Allow by Exception
implementation_statement: Cloud and payments segments deny by default and allow by exception.
TLS 1.2 or higher for all web and API traffic; private circuits to the core processor; IPsec between sites and the cloud.
Customer-managed keys for production data stores; backup keys are separate.
Approved algorithms through provider services; the cryptography standard (STD-06) is due 2027-03-31.

provider_if_inherited: Cloud provider; core processor; digital banking provider
implementation_statement: Encryption at rest for cloud data stores, laptops, and provider-hosted data.
Monthly patching; critical patches within 30 days (14 days for internet-facing). Gap: 18% of on-premises servers missed the target in the first half of 2026 (R-015).
EDR on all managed endpoints and servers, monitored 24x7 by the MSSP.

The SIEM monitors identity, endpoint, firewall, and cloud events. Gaps: payments hub, correspondent portal, and core security events are not monitored, and there are no use cases for beneficiary, template, limit, or contact changes (gap 7; R-013).
Egress from the production account passes the cloud firewall with alerting on new destinations; on-premises egress volume is not alerted.
The ISO receives FS-ISAC, CISA, and vendor advisories and tracks actions weekly.
Payments hub software and the AI model container are signed and hashed at release; file integrity monitoring on the payments workstations.
The payments hub validates wire fields (routing numbers, amounts, beneficiary names) and screens against sanctions lists before release.
Records are kept under the retention schedule; security documentation for at least 5 years (POL-01 statement 4.13).
The third-party risk policy serves as the supply chain plan; it does not address software suppliers such as the payments hub vendor.
Supplier controls are set by tier at onboarding; ongoing monitoring is annual for Tier 1 only.
Hardware is bought from authorized resellers; software from vendors with signed releases.
Tier 1 vendors are reassessed each year through SOC reports; reviews did not map CUECs or follow up on exceptions except for the core processor (P09).
